coffeeFruit.label: The coffee fruit
coffeeFruit.title: The other half of coffee
coffeeFruit.intro: The other half of coffee is the pulp of the coffee cherry. That fruit is exactly what Cafété puts at the centre.
coffeeFruit.tasteBody: Fruity notes, light floral aromas, a delicate natural sweetness and a gentle acidity define the taste. The finish recalls red berries and rosehip — not classic coffee.
coffeeFruit.traditionBody: An infusion of dried coffee fruit has been enjoyed for generations across coffee-growing regions. CAFÉTÉ carries on that tradition and brings it into a new form.
coffeeFruit.originBody: Our coffee fruit comes from Brazil – a country whose culture and agriculture have been shaped by coffee for almost 300 years.

project.label: The product
project.title: The project
project.body: CAFÉTÉ is a sparkling drink based on the coffee fruit. Its base is a real infusion of dried coffee fruit — no extract, no flavouring. Added to that: cranberry and elderberry juice, a little beet sugar and carbonation. Bottled in a 33 cl glass bottle, pasteurised, developed and produced in Switzerland.

functional.title: Functional
functional.body: For active moments in everyday life — at the office, on the go or during sport. Sparkling, refreshing, with natural caffeine from the coffee fruit. At 4.5 g of sugar per 100 ml, CAFÉTÉ has over 50 % less sugar than conventional soft drinks.

social.title: Social
social.body: Around 10 million tonnes of coffee beans are produced worldwide each year — and with them a correspondingly huge amount of coffee fruit. Using it creates value from a part of the harvest that until now brought little return and could mostly only be used locally.

ecological.title: Ecological
ecological.body: Every drink needs a raw material — and almost every raw material needs land. The coffee fruit doesn’t: it grows anyway, about 2.0–2.3 kg per kilogram of coffee beans. For CAFÉTÉ, no additional land is planted, irrigated or fertilised. We work with what is already there.

economic.title: Economic
economic.body: The coffee fruit is still often underestimated. CAFÉTÉ turns it into a premium drink — and shows that this raw material holds a market of its own.

story.label: Our story
story.title: How it all began
story.p1: CAFÉTÉ began three years ago in a claro shop, where Kareem — a passionate hospitality professional of some twenty years and one of the two founders — spotted a large glass jar full of dried, reddish fruit. He couldn’t say what it was. When he asked, he learned: it’s part of the coffee plant. His curiosity was sparked — and since hardly anyone asked about it back then, he was given a handful to try.
story.p2: At home he brewed his first infusion from it: fruity, slightly tart and surprisingly distinct. The more Kareem learned about the coffee fruit, the clearer it became that there was far more to it.
story.p3: Three years later, a handful of coffee fruit became CAFÉTÉ.
story.teaser: Within three years, a handful of coffee fruit became Cafété.

vision.label: The vision
vision.title: A category of its own
vision.body: CAFÉTÉ wants to establish the coffee fruit as a category of its own in Switzerland — not a niche product for connoisseurs, but a fixture on the shelf. We believe the coffee fruit deserves more attention. With CAFÉTÉ, we make a raw material rich in tradition experienceable in a new way.

kareem.name: Kareem Oueini
kareem.bio: Kareem Oueini is a trained chef and food craftsman by passion. He has worked in hospitality for some two decades, developing a fine instinct for taste, balance and quality. He brings that experience to CAFÉTÉ — especially in recipe development, where the interplay of aromas, sweetness, acidity and structure is decisive. A nature-loving and sporty person, he has also long been interested in nutrition, hydration and the quality of what we put into our bodies.

hannes.name: Hannes-Valentin Juon
hannes.bio: Through his qualification as a Technical Business Specialist (Technischer Kaufmann FA), Hannes-Valentin Juon has a solid grounding in business and a practical feel for numbers and commercial context. At CAFÉTÉ he handles the commercial side: financial planning, pricing and — together with Kareem — the company’s overall direction. He is also interested in digitalisation and operations, and wants to build CAFÉTÉ step by step into a stable, locally rooted company.

items.q: What is the coffee fruit — and does CAFÉTÉ taste like coffee?
items.a: The coffee bean is the seed of a fruit. The red pulp around it is called cascara. CAFÉTÉ is made from a real infusion of that dried fruit, so it doesn’t taste like coffee but fruity — the finish leans towards red berries and rosehip.

items.q: How much caffeine is in it?
items.a: About as much as an espresso. CAFÉTÉ naturally contains caffeine from the coffee fruit.

items.q: How much sugar is in it?
items.a: Over 50 % less than in conventional soft drinks — 4.5 g per 100 ml.
Yes. CAFÉTÉ contains only plant-based ingredients.
Cool and dark. CAFÉTÉ is at its best well chilled — that’s when the fruit notes and the carbonation come through most clearly.
At launch we ship within Switzerland. Shipping is included in the price.

items.q: Can I return or exchange an order?
items.a: We do not take back correctly delivered food and beverages — Swiss law provides no general right of withdrawal for them. If a delivery arrives damaged, defective or incorrect, do get in touch: we will look into it and, where a complaint is justified, arrange an appropriate solution. The details are on the Returns & Withdrawal page.

portraits.label: The portrait series
portraits.title: The other half of the story
intro: The coffee bean has a name, an origin and a value. It is selected, graded, roasted and celebrated.
The coffee fruit it grows in is usually removed before anyone even asks about it.

If you compare our society to a coffee plant, there is a great deal that is seen, shared, said and decided. But there is just as much that goes unseen, unshared and unsaid — and decisions that ought to be made but never become a topic at all.

Our society tends to look at what is already visible: known names, big stages, successful stories. We hear less about those who are still at the beginning, who work in the background, who have failed, who have started again, or whose needs have so far been given little room.
“The other half of the story” gives people and projects exactly that room. Every month. Month after month.
We already know one half of the story. Here you will find the other.
portraits.closing: Because our stage belongs to the coffee fruit — not the coffee bean.
